1.name: Body
1.note: Holds the air path. The Ø20 venturi throat is where the air speeds up and its pressure drops, which is what draws the fuel.

2.name: Float bowl
2.note: The fuel reservoir under the body. It is vented to the air horn, so the fuel surface sits at ambient pressure while the throat sits below it.

3.name: Bowl gasket
3.note: Seals the bowl to the body so petrol cannot weep out at the joint.

4.name: Bowl screw
4.note: Two screws that clamp the bowl and gasket up against the body.

5.name: Drain plug
5.note: Closes the bottom of the bowl. Unscrew it to drain old fuel and dirt.

6.name: Sealing washer
6.note: A soft copper ring that crushes under the drain plug to seal it.

7.name: Main jet
7.note: A calibrated Ø1.35 hole that meters the fuel. Its size sets how much petrol a given throat depression lifts.

8.name: Emulsion tube
8.note: A drilled tube in the main well. Air from the main air jet bleeds in through its holes and froths the fuel before it reaches the nozzle.

9.name: Main nozzle
9.note: Stands in the middle of the throat and spills the fuel into the fastest air, where the depression is greatest.

10.name: Main air jet
10.note: Feeds the emulsion tube. It stops the mixture running ever richer as the air flow rises, so fuel follows air in proportion.

11.name: Pilot jet
11.note: Meters fuel for the idle circuit. It is the only fuel supply until the throat depression is strong enough to feed the main nozzle.

12.name: Pilot air jet
12.note: Lets air into the pilot passage, where it meets the pilot fuel and sets how lean the idle mixture is.

13.name: Mixture screw
13.note: A tapered needle over the idle port. Turning it in or out changes the idle opening, so it trims the idle mixture.

14.name: Screw spring
14.note: Presses on the mixture screw so vibration cannot turn it and shift the setting.

15.name: Float
15.note: Floats on the fuel in the bowl. As the level falls it drops and lifts the needle off its seat to let more petrol in.

16.name: Float arm
16.note: A lever from the float to the needle. It sets how far the needle travels for each millimetre the float moves.

17.name: Hinge pin
17.note: The pivot the float arm swings on.

18.name: Float needle
18.note: The inlet valve. Its soft tip seats in the Ø1.5 orifice when the bowl is full and lifts to refill it as the jets draw fuel off.

19.name: Needle seat
19.note: The Ø1.5 orifice the float needle closes. Fuel from the tank passes through it into the bowl.

20.name: Choke plate
20.note: Closes off the air horn for cold starts so the depression stays high. Its two Ø6.5 holes let some air through.

21.name: Choke spindle
21.note: The shaft that turns the choke plate.

22.name: Throttle plate
22.note: Sets the air flow, and so the engine's power. Cut slightly oval so it seals in the bore when closed.

23.name: Throttle spindle
23.note: The shaft that turns the throttle plate. As the plate opens its edge sweeps the progression ports in turn.

24.name: Ball plug
24.note: Steel balls pressed in to seal the ends of drilled passages.

25.name: Bowl vent tube
25.note: Connects the bowl to the air horn, so the fuel surface sees the same pressure as the air entering the throat.

26.name: Fuel inlet nipple
26.note: Takes the fuel line from the tank and feeds the needle seat.
